course.title: Swimming Basics
course.tagline: Learn to swim with confidence: floating, strokes and water safety.

days.title: Water safety first
days.goal: Learn the safety rules before you get in the water.

video.title: How to Swim in 3 Days | Beginner Swimming Lessons with Jonny Rocket

steps: Watch the video and write the main safety rule in your own words.
Rule 1: never swim alone. Rule 2: swim where a lifeguard is on duty.
Learn where the shallow end of your pool is.
Tell a friend the safety rules.
days.task: Write the 2 safety rules on a card.
days.challenge: Find a pool with a lifeguard near you.

quiz.q: What is the first safety rule?
quiz.explain: Never swim alone keeps you safe.

quiz.q: Why swim where a lifeguard is?
options: A lifeguard can help fast if you struggle
quiz.explain: A lifeguard watches and helps.

quiz.q: What should you learn about your pool?
quiz.explain: Knowing the shallow end keeps you safe.

days.title: Get comfortable in the water
days.goal: Spend time in shallow water and get used to it.

video.title: LEARN to swim CONFIDENT, FLOAT & BE WATER SAFE in 3 Steps

steps: Walk in waist-deep water for 5 minutes.
Splash water on your face and arms.
Hold the pool edge and bob up and down.
Breathe slowly and relax.
days.task: Walk in shallow water for 5 minutes.
days.challenge: Bob up and down holding the edge 10 times.

options: You can stand and feel safe
quiz.explain: Shallow water lets you learn safely.

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel scared?
options: Breathe slowly and hold the edge
quiz.explain: Slow breathing and holding on calms fear.

options: It teaches you how water lifts you
quiz.explain: Bobbing builds water confidence.

days.title: Blow bubbles: breathe out in water
days.goal: Learn to breathe out under water.

video.title: How to SWIM and FLOATS (Beginner Tutorial)

steps: Stand in shallow water and take a breath.
Put your mouth in the water and blow bubbles slowly.
Then put your nose in and blow bubbles.
Then put your whole face in and blow bubbles.
days.task: Blow bubbles 10 times today.
days.challenge: Blow bubbles with your whole face in.

options: It teaches you to breathe out under water
quiz.explain: Blowing bubbles is the base of swim breathing.

quiz.q: What should you breathe out through?
quiz.explain: Breathing out through nose and mouth clears water.

quiz.q: Why put your face in slowly?
options: So you get used to it step by step
quiz.explain: Slow steps build confidence.

days.title: Float on your back
days.goal: Learn to float on your back and trust the water.

video.title: How to Do the Front Crawl / Freestyle Swimming Stroke

steps: Hold the pool edge and lean back.
Let your ears go in the water and look up.
Push your hips up and spread your arms out.
Relax and let the water hold you for 5 seconds.
days.task: Float on your back for 5 seconds.
days.challenge: Float on your back for 10 seconds.

quiz.q: Why float on your back first?
options: It is the easiest float and builds trust
quiz.explain: Back floating shows you the water holds you.
Ears in the water helps you float flat.
Hips up keeps your body flat on the water.

days.title: Float on your front
days.goal: Learn to float face down.

video.title: Breaking Down the Freestyle Stroke Technique

steps: Hold the pool edge and stretch out face down.
Keep your face in the water and blow bubbles.
Let your legs rise behind you.
Hold the float for 5 seconds, then stand up.
days.task: Float on your front for 5 seconds.
days.challenge: Float on your front for 10 seconds.

quiz.q: What should you do with your face?
options: Keep it in the water and blow bubbles
quiz.explain: Face in and bubbles keep you calm.
Legs up keep your body flat.

quiz.q: How do you stand up from a front float?
options: Tuck your knees, push your arms down, lift your head
quiz.explain: Tucking knees brings your feet under you.

days.title: Kick with a board
days.goal: Learn the flutter kick with a kickboard.

video.title: How to Swim Freestyle

steps: Hold a kickboard in front of you.
Kick from your hips with nearly straight legs.
Point your toes like a dancer.
Kick for 10 metres, then rest.
days.task: Kick 10 metres with a board.
days.challenge: Kick 20 metres with a board.

options: Kicking from the hips with nearly straight legs
quiz.explain: A flutter kick moves you forward.

quiz.q: Where should the kick come from?
quiz.explain: Kicking from the hips is strong and smooth.
Pointed toes cut through water.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Float and kick
days.goal: Put week 1 together: float on your back and front, then kick.

video.title: How to Swim Freestyle for Beginners | 5-Step Guide

steps: Float on your back for 10 seconds.
Float on your front for 10 seconds.
Kick 10 metres with a board.
Write down what felt easy and what felt hard.
days.task: Do both floats and a 10-metre kick.
days.challenge: Float for 15 seconds on your back.

quiz.explain: Floating and kicking are the base of swimming.
Ten seconds shows you trust the water.

options: What felt easy and what felt hard
quiz.explain: Notes show what to practise next.

project.title: Float and kick
project.brief: Float on your back for 10 seconds, float on your front for 10 seconds, and kick 10 metres with a board, then write what felt easy and hard.

days.title: Push off and glide
days.goal: Learn to push off the wall and glide.

video.title: Smooth swimming step by step

steps: Stand at the wall and put your hands together above your head.
Push off with your feet and stretch long.
Glide as far as you can without kicking.
Add a flutter kick when the glide slows.
days.task: Glide 3 metres without kicking.
days.challenge: Glide 5 metres without kicking.

options: Sliding through water after pushing off
quiz.explain: A glide uses the push to slide forward.

quiz.q: What shape should your body be?
options: Long and straight like an arrow
quiz.explain: A long shape cuts through water.
Kicking after the glide keeps you moving.

days.title: Freestyle arms, step by step
days.goal: Learn freestyle arm strokes.

video.title: How to Float in Water: Beginner Swimming Tips

steps: Reach one arm forward into the water.
Pull it back under your body.
Lift it out and reach forward again.
Alternate arms slowly, then add the kick.
days.task: Do 10 freestyle arm strokes holding a board.
days.challenge: Swim 10 metres of freestyle arms with a kick.

options: A stroke with alternating arms and a flutter kick
quiz.explain: Freestyle is the fastest common stroke.

quiz.q: How should your arm enter the water?
quiz.explain: Reaching forward makes a smooth entry.

quiz.q: What should your arm do under water?
quiz.explain: Pulling back moves you forward.

days.title: Breathe to the side
days.goal: Learn to breathe while swimming freestyle.

video.title: How to Swim for Beginners | Step-by-Step Swimming Lessons with Jonny Rocket & Ada

steps: Swim freestyle and turn your head to the side to breathe.
Keep one ear in the water as you turn.
Breathe in quickly, then put your face back in.
Breathe every 3 strokes.
days.task: Swim 10 metres breathing every 3 strokes.
days.challenge: Swim 15 metres breathing to the side.

quiz.q: How do you breathe in freestyle?
options: Turn your head to the side
quiz.explain: Turning to the side keeps your body flat.
One ear in keeps your head low.
Every 3 strokes gives steady air.

days.title: Backstroke basics
days.goal: Learn backstroke, swimming on your back.

video.title: How to Swim For Beginners | Kerima Learns To Swim with Jonny Rocket

steps: Lie on your back and float.
Move your arms in circles, one at a time.
Kick gently from your hips.
Look up at the sky or ceiling.
days.task: Swim 10 metres of backstroke.
days.challenge: Swim 15 metres of backstroke.

options: Swimming on your back with alternating arms
quiz.explain: Backstroke is swimming on your back.

quiz.q: Where should you look in backstroke?
options: Up at the sky or ceiling
quiz.explain: Looking up keeps your body flat.

options: In circles, one at a time
quiz.explain: Alternating arm circles move you forward.

days.title: Tread water
days.goal: Learn to tread water: stay up in deep water.

video.title: How to Float in Water for Beginners | Swim on Your Back in 4 Steps

steps: Move your legs in a cycling motion.
Move your hands in small circles to push water down.
Keep your head above water and breathe normally.
Tread for 30 seconds.
days.task: Tread water for 30 seconds.
days.challenge: Tread water for 1 minute.

options: Staying up in deep water without swimming
quiz.explain: Treading keeps you up in deep water.
Cycling legs keep you up.

options: Push water down in small circles
quiz.explain: Hands pushing down lift you up.

days.title: Breaststroke kick
days.goal: Learn the breaststroke frog kick.

video.title: LEARN TO SWIM | Ep.1 Building Water Comfort | Breath control, sculling, safety skills for beginners

steps: Bend your knees and bring your heels toward your body.
Turn your feet out.
Kick out and around in a circle, then snap your legs together.
Practise holding the wall first.
days.task: Do 10 frog kicks holding the wall.
days.challenge: Do 10 frog kicks with a board.

options: Bending knees, turning feet out, kicking in a circle
quiz.explain: A frog kick powers breaststroke.
Feet out catch the water.
Snapping together finishes the kick.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Swim 25 metres
days.goal: Put week 2 together: swim 25 metres of freestyle.

video.title: How to Swim in 3 Days | Beginner Swimming Lessons with Jonny Rocket

steps: Warm up with a float and a kick.
Swim freestyle for 25 metres, breathing to the side.
Rest at the wall, then swim back.
Write down how it felt.
days.task: Swim 25 metres of freestyle.
days.challenge: Swim 25 metres twice with a rest.

options: One length of a short pool
quiz.explain: Twenty-five metres is one pool length.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get tired?
options: Stop at the wall and rest
quiz.explain: Resting at the wall is safe.
Notes show what to improve.

project.title: Swim 25 metres
project.brief: Swim 25 metres of freestyle breathing to the side, rest, then swim back, and write how it felt.

days.title: Swim with a friend
days.goal: Swim with a friend for safety and fun.

video.title: LEARN to swim CONFIDENT, FLOAT & BE WATER SAFE in 3 Steps

steps: Pick a friend to swim with you.
Stay in the shallow end together.
Take turns swimming a length.
Watch each other and cheer each other on.
days.task: Swim with a friend this week.
days.challenge: Teach a friend to float.

options: It is safer and more fun
quiz.explain: A friend adds safety and fun.

quiz.q: Where should you stay with a friend?
options: In the shallow end at first
quiz.explain: Shallow water is safe for learning.

quiz.q: What should you do while your friend swims?
quiz.explain: Watching keeps your friend safe.

days.title: Improve your freestyle
days.goal: Make your freestyle smoother and longer.

video.title: How to SWIM and FLOATS (Beginner Tutorial)

steps: Reach further forward with each arm.
Kick steadily, not hard.
Breathe every 3 strokes.
Swim 25 metres and count your strokes.
days.task: Swim 25 metres and count your strokes.
days.challenge: Swim 25 metres with fewer strokes than last time.

quiz.explain: Long strokes are smooth and efficient.

quiz.q: How should you kick in freestyle?
quiz.explain: A steady kick keeps you moving.
Fewer strokes show better technique.

days.title: Learn to dive safely
days.goal: Learn a safe shallow dive from the pool edge.

video.title: How to Do the Front Crawl / Freestyle Swimming Stroke

steps: Only dive where the water is deep enough.
Sit on the edge and slide in head first.
Keep your arms stretched above your head.
Practise with a teacher watching.
days.task: Practise a sitting dive with a teacher.
days.challenge: Slide in head first from the edge.

options: Only where the water is deep enough
quiz.explain: Deep water only is safe for diving.

quiz.q: What shape should your body be?
options: Long and straight, arms above your head
quiz.explain: A long shape enters the water safely.
A teacher keeps diving safe.

days.title: Swim longer: build stamina
days.goal: Build up to swimming for 5 minutes without stopping.

video.title: Breaking Down the Freestyle Stroke Technique

steps: Swim slowly for 2 minutes, rest, repeat.
Add 1 minute each session.
Breathe every 3 strokes.
Write down your longest swim.
days.task: Swim for 3 minutes without stopping.
days.challenge: Swim for 5 minutes without stopping.

options: Add a little time each session
quiz.explain: Small adds build stamina safely.

quiz.q: What pace should a long swim be?
quiz.explain: Slow and steady lasts longer.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get tired?
quiz.explain: Resting at the wall is safe.

days.title: Water safety: what to do if you struggle
days.goal: Learn what to do if you get into trouble in water.

video.title: How to Swim Freestyle

steps: Stay calm and float on your back.
Wave one arm and shout for help.
Do not grab the person trying to help you.
If you see someone struggle, call for help, do not jump in.
days.task: Practise floating on your back for 30 seconds.
days.challenge: Tell a friend the 3 safety steps.

quiz.q: What should you do if you struggle?
options: Stay calm and float on your back
quiz.explain: Floating calmly saves energy.

quiz.q: What should you do to get help?
quiz.explain: Waving and shouting brings help.

quiz.q: What should you do if you see someone struggle?
options: Call for help, do not jump in
quiz.explain: Calling for help is the safe rescue.

days.title: Practise all strokes
days.goal: Swim freestyle, backstroke and breaststroke in one session.

video.title: How to Swim Freestyle for Beginners | 5-Step Guide

steps: Swim 25 metres freestyle.
Swim 25 metres backstroke.
Swim 25 metres breaststroke kick with a board.
Rest between each one.
days.task: Swim all 3 strokes today.
days.challenge: Swim your weakest stroke twice.

quiz.explain: Different strokes build all-round swimming.

quiz.q: What should you do between strokes?
quiz.explain: Rest keeps each stroke good.

quiz.q: Which stroke should you practise most?
quiz.explain: Practising the weak stroke makes you balanced.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Swim 50 metres
days.goal: Put week 3 together: swim 50 metres without stopping.

video.title: Smooth swimming step by step

steps: Warm up with a float and a kick.
Swim 50 metres of freestyle, breathing every 3 strokes.
Rest, then swim 25 metres of backstroke.
Write down your time and how you felt.
days.task: Swim 50 metres of freestyle.
days.challenge: Swim 50 metres twice with a rest.

options: Two lengths of a short pool
quiz.explain: Fifty metres is two pool lengths.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get tired?
options: Rest at the wall, then continue
quiz.explain: Resting is safe.

options: Your time and how you felt
quiz.explain: Notes show progress.

project.title: Swim 50 metres
project.brief: Swim 50 metres of freestyle breathing every 3 strokes, rest, then swim 25 metres of backstroke.

days.title: Swim with good breathing
days.goal: Practise breathing every 3 strokes for a full length.

video.title: How to Float in Water: Beginner Swimming Tips

steps: Swim 25 metres breathing every 3 strokes.
Keep your head low when you breathe.
Breathe out slowly under water.
Write down how many breaths you took.
days.task: Swim 25 metres breathing every 3 strokes.
days.challenge: Swim 50 metres breathing every 3 strokes.

options: It is a rule with no reason
It keeps breathing steady and balanced
quiz.explain: Every 3 strokes gives steady air.

quiz.q: What should you do under water?
quiz.explain: Breathing out under water prepares the next breath.

quiz.q: Where should your head be when breathing?
options: Low, one ear in the water
quiz.explain: A low head keeps your body flat.

days.title: Open water safety
days.goal: Learn the extra rules for lakes, rivers and the sea.

video.title: How to Swim for Beginners | Step-by-Step Swimming Lessons with Jonny Rocket & Ada

steps: Never swim alone in open water.
Check the depth and the current before entering.
Stay close to shore.
Get out if you feel cold or tired.
days.task: Write the 4 open-water rules on a card.
days.challenge: Tell a friend the open-water rules.

quiz.explain: Open water is natural water outside a pool.

options: Strong water can pull you away
quiz.explain: A strong current can carry you away.

options: If you feel cold or tired
quiz.explain: Cold or tired means get out.

days.title: Keep swimming: your routine
days.goal: Make swimming a weekly habit.

video.title: How to Swim For Beginners | Kerima Learns To Swim with Jonny Rocket

steps: Swim 2 times a week.
Each session: warm-up, strokes, cool-down.
Set a new goal: swim 100 metres.
Write your weekly swim plan.
days.task: Write your weekly swim plan.
days.challenge: Swim twice this week.

quiz.explain: Twice a week keeps the habit alive.
A full session warms up, works and cools down.

quiz.q: What is a good next goal?
quiz.explain: A new goal keeps you growing.

days.title: Teach a friend to float
days.goal: Teach someone else to float on their back.

video.title: How to Float in Water for Beginners | Swim on Your Back in 4 Steps

steps: Show them how to lean back and relax.
Support their head and back at first.
Let go slowly when they feel safe.
Cheer them on.
days.task: Teach one person to float.
days.challenge: Support a friend's first float.

options: Teaching helps you learn it better
quiz.explain: Teaching locks in your own learning.
Supporting head and back builds trust.

options: When they feel safe and relaxed
quiz.explain: Letting go slowly builds confidence.

days.title: Swim with a kickboard: build your legs
days.goal: Learn to build leg strength with a kickboard.

video.title: LEARN TO SWIM | Ep.1 Building Water Comfort | Breath control, sculling, safety skills for beginners

steps: Hold the kickboard with both hands.
Kick from your hips, not your knees.
Keep your legs straight but soft.
Breathe out into the water.
Kick for 25 metres, then rest.
Repeat 4 times.
days.task: Kick 25 metres with a board today.
days.challenge: Kick 50 metres without stopping.

quiz.q: Where should the kick come from?
quiz.explain: Kicking from the hips is strong and smooth.
Straight but soft legs kick best.

quiz.q: How far should you kick first?
quiz.explain: Twenty-five metres is a good first goal.

days.title: Swim in a group class
days.goal: Learn what to expect in a group swim class.

video.title: How to Swim in 3 Days | Beginner Swimming Lessons with Jonny Rocket

steps: Arrive early and tell the teacher you are a beginner.
Listen to the teacher's instructions.
Stay in the shallow end until you are sure.
Ask questions when you do not understand.
Practise what the teacher shows.
Thank the teacher at the end.
days.task: Find a group swim class near you.
days.challenge: Join one class this month.

quiz.q: What should you tell the teacher first?
quiz.explain: Telling the teacher helps them teach you right.

quiz.q: Where should you stay at first?
quiz.explain: The shallow end is safe while you learn.

quiz.q: What should you do if you do not understand?
quiz.explain: Asking keeps you safe and learning.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final swim.

video.title: LEARN to swim CONFIDENT, FLOAT & BE WATER SAFE in 3 Steps

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 skills you can now do in water.
Practise your capstone swim once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 swim skills you learned.
days.challenge: Swim your capstone distance from memory.

options: A final swim that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
quiz.explain: A safe 100-metre swim shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone swim once more, then rest.

video.title: How to SWIM and FLOATS (Beginner Tutorial)

steps: Swim your capstone distance one more time.
Check your breathing and your strokes.
Fix anything that felt hard.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Swim your capstone distance and time it.
days.challenge: Fix one hard part of your swim.

options: Practice makes the real swim calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your breathing, your strokes and your turns
quiz.explain: Checking breathing and strokes makes it smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you swim your best.

days.title: Capstone day: swim 100 metres
days.goal: Show what you learned: swim 100 metres.

video.title: How to Do the Front Crawl / Freestyle Swimming Stroke

steps: Warm up with a float and a kick.
Swim 100 metres of freestyle, breathing every 3 strokes.
Rest at the wall if you must, then continue.
Cool down and write your report.
days.task: Swim your 100 metres and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: How far is your capstone swim?
quiz.explain: The capstone is a 100-metre swim.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get tired?
options: Rest at the wall, then continue
quiz.explain: Resting is safe.

options: Your time, your strokes and how you felt
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Swim 100 metres
capstone.brief: Swim 100 metres of freestyle breathing every 3 strokes, with a warm-up and cool-down, and write a short report on your time, strokes and how you felt.
checks: Warmed up with float and kick
deliverables: A list of swim skills learned
A short video or notes from the swim
